result.topic_en: Definitions of the four theta functions, the expression of an elliptic-function quantity through $\vartheta_1$, the Jacobi imaginary transformation $q\to q'$ with $\log q\log q'=\pi^2$, a crossed-out attempt at the general linear (modular) transformation of the periods, and quasi-periodicity of $\vartheta_1$.
result.transcription:
$\vartheta(v,q)=\sum(-1)^n q^{n^2}e^{2nv}$
$\vartheta_1(v,q)=\sum(-1)^n q^{(n+\frac12)^2}e^{(2n+1)v}$
$\vartheta_2(v,q)=\sum q^{(n+\frac12)^2}e^{(2n+1)v}$
$\vartheta_3(v,q)=\sum q^{n^2}e^{2nv}$
$q=e^{-\frac{\pi\pi}{aa}t}$ ; $v=\frac{x\pi i}{2a}$
$\varsigma=\frac{2e^{-t}}{a}\sum_1^\infty(-1)^{n-1}q^{(n-\frac12)^2}$ [-...-] $\frac{e^{(2n-1)v}-e^{-(2n-1)v}}{2i}$
$=\frac{e^{-t}}{ai}\left\{\sum_1^\infty(-1)^{n-1}q^{(n-\frac12)^2}e^{(2n-1)v}-\sum_{-1}^{-\infty}(-1)^{n+1}q^{(n+\frac12)^2}e^{(2n+1)v}\right\}$
$=\frac{e^{-t}}{ai}\left\{\sum_0^\infty(-1)^n q^{(n+\frac12)^2}e^{(2n+1)v}+\sum_{-1}\right\}$
$=\frac{e^{-t}}{ai}\vartheta_1(v,q)$
$\log q\log q'=+\pi\pi$ ; $\frac{\pi i}{\log q}=-\frac{\log q'}{\pi i}$
$q=e^{2\pi\varsigma i}$ (pag. 128) ; $\varsigma=\frac{\omega'}{\omega}=r+si$ ; $s>0$ (pag. 84)
$g\omega=4K$ (pag. 96) ; $g\omega'=2K'i$ (pag. 120)
also $q=e^{-\frac{\pi K'}{K}}$
$v=\frac{2\pi i z}{\omega}$ ; $g=1$
$e^{\frac{zv}{\omega'}}$ [-...-] $=e^{\frac{\omega v^2}{2\pi i\omega'}}=e^{\frac{v^2}{2\pi i\varsigma}}$
$=e^{\frac{[-...-]v^2}{\log q}}$
$v'=v\cdot\frac{\log q'}{\pi i}$ ; $v=v'\frac{\pi i}{\log q}=-v'\frac{\log q'}{\pi i}$
$\vartheta_1(v',q')=e^{\frac{v^2}{\log q}}\vartheta_1(v,q)$
$\frac{v^2}{\log q}+\frac{v'^2}{\log q'}=\frac{v^2}{\log q}+\frac{v^2\log q'^2}{-\pi^2\log q'}$ | $\varsigma=\frac{K'i}{2K}$
[-$\vartheta_1\left(\frac{\alpha\pi i+\beta\log q}{\gamma\pi i+\delta\log q}\right)$ ... $\left(\frac{\gamma\pi i+\delta\log q}{\alpha\pi i+\beta\log q}\right)=$ ...-]
[-Allgemeine Transformation-]
[-$\omega=-\alpha\log q+\beta\pi i$ | $\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma=+1$-]
[-$\omega'=-\gamma\log q+\delta\pi i$-]
[-$\frac{-\gamma\log q+\delta\pi i}{-\alpha\log q+\beta\pi i}=\frac{\pi i}{-\log q'}$-]
$\log q=2\pi i\frac{\omega'}{\omega}=+\pi i\cdot\frac{K'i}{K}$
$\pi i$ die erste, $\log q$ die zweite Periode
$\frac{\pi i}{\log q'}=\frac{\alpha\pi i+\beta\log q}{\gamma\pi i+\delta\log q}$ | $\frac{\log q'}{\pi i}=\lambda'=\frac{\gamma+\delta\lambda}{\alpha+\beta\lambda}$
$\frac{\pi i}{\log q}=\frac{\delta\pi i-\beta\log q'}{-\gamma\pi i+\alpha\log q'}$
$\alpha\lambda'+\beta\lambda\lambda'=\gamma+\delta\lambda$
$\alpha'\lambda+\beta'\lambda\lambda'=\gamma'+\delta'\lambda'$
$\vartheta_1(v+\pi i)=-\vartheta_1(v)$ \quad $\vartheta_1(-v)=-\vartheta_1(v)$
$\vartheta_1(v+\log q)=\sum(-1)^n q^{(n+\frac12)^2+2(n+\frac12)}e^{(2n+1)v}$ | $v=0$
$=\sum(-1)^n q^{(n+\frac32)^2-1}e^{(2n+1)v}$
$=-q^{-1}e^{-2v}\vartheta_1(v)$
$=q^{-1}e^{-2v}\vartheta_1(-v)$
